defect.description: Input_args given as ordinary ffmpeg arguments in a string rather than a preset name (for example '-rtsp_transport tcp') are concatenated as a str onto the argument list: get_ffmpeg_arg_list(...) + '-rtsp_transport tcp' raises TypeError (can only concatenate list to list), so audio detection fails to start; the fallbacks need get_ffmpeg_arg_list(...) like the global args.

review_items: src/audio.py:17,19 - string input_args fallbacks not passed through get_ffmpeg_arg_list (plain string like '-rtsp_transport tcp' mishandled)
src/audio.py:16,18 - detect_fps hardcoded to 1 for audio inputs
tests/test_audio.py - no test covering plain-string input_args
votes.evidence_quote: The fallbacks `or ffmpeg_input.input_args` (line 17) and `or ffmpeg.input_args` (line 19) pass a string directly into the command list. When `input_args` is a plain ffmpeg string like `"-rtsp_transport tcp"` ... Should read `or get_ffmpeg_arg_list(ffmpeg_input.input_args)`.
votes.justification: The review flags the same faulty fallbacks in get_ffmpeg_command, where plain-string input_args is not run through get_ffmpeg_arg_list, and it proposes the correct fix. It misdescribes the outcome as a single malformed argument rather than a TypeError from list+str concatenation, but the cause, location and fix all match.
